dispositions.topic_text: Exact OWNER_FORM_FIELDS rows and their field, path, carrier, and kind mappings
dispositions.what: The exact rows of the owner form table, each field's path, its tuple position mark and its carrier, are State 6's: the data provider's owner form table and 60_contracts.md's owner form paragraph. Options: one row per leaf field of the owner request and its values; or rows generated from the models. Consequences: an explicit table is reviewed as data; a generated one can drift silently. Every option must keep: a page and the reader name every field alike.
keeps: The table holds the names so that the page and the reader cannot name a field differently (Route B runs of 2026-11-25).
options: State 6 explicitly declares every OWNER_FORM_FIELDS row alongside the owner contracts.
State 6 declares the owner contracts and derives every row by a complete deterministic rule.
consequences: Explicit rows expose every external name but duplicate contract information.
Derivation avoids duplication but must unambiguously cover nested and tuple-valued inputs.

dispositions.topic_text: How member-valued rows identify their enumeration
dispositions.what: A member row's enumeration is the declared type of the field its path reaches in the model it fills (State 6 models). Options: by the destination field's type; or by an enumeration column in the row. Consequences: the first needs no extra column; the second duplicates the model. Every option must keep: a member's text is read as exactly one member's value.
keeps:
the vocabularies reach the code as the model
enumerations State 6 declares.
options: Infer the enumeration from the typed destination field in the State 6 contract.
Add the enumeration identity as another fact of each member-valued OWNER_FORM_FIELDS row.
consequences: Typed inference requires every destination path to resolve to one enumeration.
An explicit enumeration fact makes each row self-contained but duplicates type information.

dispositions.topic_text: OWNER_FORM_FIELDS name-uniqueness invariant and release test
dispositions.what: Before admission, a check proves that no two rows of the owner form table share a name. Options: check the source table; check the generated constant; or both. Every option must keep: the name alone picks a row.
keeps:
No two rows share a name: the name alone
picks a row, and a table in which two rows share one is not a release.
options: Add a factory check that rejects any OWNER_FORM_FIELDS table with duplicate names.
Express pairwise uniqueness in the generated schema and have the factory validate that schema.
consequences: Either mechanism must reject the candidate release before it can run.

dispositions.topic_text: Page-reader field-name agreement invariant and test
dispositions.what: A check proves that every field an owner page writes is named by a row of the owner form table and that every row the reader uses for an action is written by its page. Options: a structural check of the generated module; a round-trip test that renders and reads each form; or both. Every option must keep: the page and the reader agree on every field name.
keeps:
The table holds the names
so that the page and the reader cannot name a field differently (Route B
runs of 2026-11-25).
options: Require a complete page-to-reader round-trip check for every row and owner action.
Require a structural check proving both page emission and request reading obtain names only from the same complete table.
consequences: Round-trip checks demonstrate the visible agreement through generated cases.
A structural check is smaller but must establish that neither side has another source of names.

dispositions.topic_text: Representation of multipart file uploads in OWNER_FORM_FIELDS
dispositions.reason: The multipart file part is not a form field: its bytes reach operations as the UploadBody the upload head names (State 5 owner surface, 60_contracts.md), and only the CSRF part of an upload is read as a form value.

dispositions.topic_text: Accepted lexical forms for integer and other scalar fields
dispositions.reason: The integer kind reads only the owner request's stated version and an upload's number, which are never negative. An object's floor is a text field of the project facts (State 6 ProjectFacts.floor: str), read as text and checked by projects as A02 rule 6 says, so a floor of -1 is carried as the text -1 and stored.
